chunks.text: - Cold wave conditions very likely in isolated pockets of Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh during 5th -8th; over West Rajasthan during 5th -9th; over East Rajasthan during 5th -10th; over Jharkhand on 6th -7th January 2026. | 2 3. Inputs Situation a) Water Reservoir Status: As on 01 January 2026, the total live water storage in 166 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 142.177 billion cubic meter, which is 77.4% of total live storage capacity (183.565 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 105.58 percent of last year's storage and 122.53 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period. b) Groundwater Levels: In August 2025, In Post-monsoon 2025, around 90% of the country's monitoring stations exhibited a depth to water level within 10 meters below ground level. Deeper water levels of more than 20 m are observed in around 5% of stations of the country covering mainly the western states, especially Western Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh.

chunks.heading: Introduction
chunks.text: - The deeper groundwater level in the states like Western Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh during Post-monsoon 2025 has been significantly influenced by the over extraction of groundwater compared to the recharge during the monsoon period. - Annual water level comparison with the previous year Post-monsoon 2024 to Post- monsoon 2025 has shown that about 63% of total analyzed stations of the country experienced rise in annual water level fluctuation may be attributed to the less groundwater extraction compared to 2024. - About 73% of the analyzed stations of the unconfined aquifer experienced a rise of water level in the decadal mean water level fluctuation of 2015-2024 with respect to Post- monsoon 2025. - The Groundwater Drought Indices indicate that in Post-monsoon 2025, groundwater conditions across India remained largely stable, with 91% of monitoring stations showing no deficit. However, localized deficits were observed in several regions — notably in Meghalaya, Nagaland, and the Dadar Nagar Havili & Daman & Diu. c) Fertilizers: The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. | 3 4. Pests & Diseases: There is no major pest incidence that has been reported. The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level. 5.

chunks.heading: Details of each Segment
chunks.text:
- During the week (25 Dec – 31 Dec 2025), lower rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 95%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01st Oct to 31 Dec 2025) is higher than LPA by 11%. Rainfall Forecast: - Overall, rainfall activity is likely to be below over the country except Tamil Nadu and Kerala, where it is likely to be near normal to above normal.


Temerature Week 1 (02 Jan – 08 Jan 2026): - Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal 2-4°C over most parts of the country except northeast India & Western Himalayan Region and many parts of northwest India, where these are likely to be above normal by 1-3°C during the week.
| 5 Week 2 (09 Jan – 15 Jan 2026): - Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal 2-4°C over most parts of the country except some parts of the Western Himalayan Region, where these are likely to be above normal by 1-3°C during the week. - Cold wave conditions are likely over some parts of Punjab, Haryana, North Rajasthan, North Madhya Pradesh, interior Odisha, adjoining parts of west Jharkhand, north Chhattisgarh, and south Uttar Pradesh during some days of the week. - Dense fog conditions are likely to prevail during early morning hours in isolated pockets of north India on some days of the week.
